_about: Numeric thresholds read by the verifier (2026-11-14) from the fetched PDFs. Page numbers are PDF page indices of the fetched files. Nothing here is from memory; where a figure was not found in a fetched document it is listed under not_found.

NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev C.title: NASA Spaceflight Human-System Standard Volume 1: Crew Health, Revision C, approved 2023-09-15, 87 pages

OCHMO-STD-100.1A.title: NASA Space Flight Medical Selection, Recertification and Mission Evaluation Standards, Revision A, release 09/09/2024, 103 pages
OCHMO-STD-100.1A.note: the NTRS copy (OCHMO STD 100 1A 05142024.pdf, 96 pages) is an earlier unsigned draft with the same text

OCHMO-TB-031.title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief: Exercise Overview, dated 10/02/2023 on each page, 26 pages

vo2_in_mission_min_microgravity_eva_ml_k.quote: Crewmembers shall maintain an in-mission VO2max at or above 32.9 ml/min/kg for missions with microgravity EVAs

vo2_in_mission_min_fraction_of_premissio.quote: at or above 80% of the pre-mission capacity
vo2_in_mission_min_fraction_of_premissio.rationale_page_34: assumes average 15% decline in VO2max and showed decrements up to 20% do not impair mission objectives

vo2_premission_recommendation_ml_kg_min.note: recommendations, not requirements; rationale p.32: 'historical experience showing declines of 15-25% in VO2max'

vo2_postflight_decline_typical_pct.quote: Aerobic capacity can be decreased by approximately 10%-30% after spaceflight depending on duration and conditions

muscle_strength_in_mission_min_fraction_.quote: Countermeasures shall maintain in-mission skeletal muscle strength at or above 80% of baseline values

muscle_strength_postflight_decline_typic.quote: Lower body muscle cross-sectional area and strength can be decreased by approximately 10-30% after spaceflight

premission_strength_table.note: deadlift/bench press, not isokinetic torque: cannot be applied to the dynamometer measures without a conversion that no fetched document gives

bmd_in_mission_min_fraction_hip_spine.quote: maintain bone mineral density of the hip and spine at or above 95% of pre-mission values and at or above 90% for the femoral neck

bmd_6_month_iss_with_countermeasures.quote: the majority of crewmembers returning with <10% deficit bone mineral density in femoral neck and <5% in total hip or spine during 6-month ISS missions

bmd_premission_tscore.quote: pre-mission bone mineral density (BMD) T-scores for total hip and lumbar spine (L1-L4) ... shall be consistent with an age, sex, gender, and ethnic-matched population

osteoporosis_tscore_disqualifying.section: Appendix, item 17 Disqualifications for Abnormal Bone Mineral Density
osteoporosis_tscore_disqualifying.quote: T-score <= -2.5 at the femoral neck, total hip, or lumbar spine using the female, white, age 20-29 ... as the reference population standard

low_bmd_zscore_disqualifying.quote: Bone mineral density below the expected range for age (Z-score < -2.0)

hypertension_definition_mmHg.quote: Hypertension, as defined by sustained systolic blood pressure of 140 mmHg or greater or diastolic of 90 mmHg or greater

bradycardia_review_bpm.quote: Prolonged sinus pause > 3 seconds or heart rate < 30 beats per minute not during sleep
bradycardia_review_bpm.note: requires AMB review and may be disqualifying

in_flight_schedule.table: Table 8 Mission Medical Examinations for Assigned Crew on > 30-day Missions
in_flight_schedule.strength_conditioning_[6025]: in-flight L+14 days (NET 3rd session) and then at least every 30 days thereafter (p.51); Resistance 3x/wk (60 min) Aerobic 3x/wk (30 min)
in_flight_schedule.bone_densitometry_[6013]: AME L-21/18 m; L-180/30 d; R+ <30 days, R+1 year, then as clinically indicated (p.45)
in_flight_schedule.functional_fitness_[6024]: AME L-9/6 m, L-90/30 d; R+5/7 d, R+30 d (p.36, p.51: includes isokinetic testing)

postflight_reconditioning_window_days.quote: return to preflight values for aerobic capacity and muscle strength during the rehabilitation period within 45 days postflight

bmd_recovery_time.quote: for many crewmembers, it requires a year to recover back to preflight values

bedrest_70d_control_vo2_decline_pct.quote: Peak aerobic capacity was maintained from pre to post bed rest in all exercise groups compared to a 10% decline in controlled group

bedrest_10d_vo2_decline_pct.quote: Previous bed rest study showed 14% decline after 10-day bed rest (no exercise)

bedrest_10d_vo2_decline_pct_convertino.quote: Convertino et al. (1997) demonstrated a 6-16% reduction in VO2max after 10 days of bedrest

not_found: A '>=20% VO2 drop = performance loss' statement: not in OCHMO-TB-031 as such; the 80% floor [V1 4003] and its rationale ('decrements up to 20% do not impair mission objectives', NASA-STD-3001 V1 p.34) are the closest text.
Bone loss rate in %/month for spaceflight (e.g. '1-1.5% per month'): not in any of the three fetched documents.

Any in-flight limit for resting heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2 or HRV: none in the three documents (OCHMO-STD-100.1A only lists vital signs as examined, p.38, and the selection-level hypertension/bradycardia definitions above).
Isokinetic torque thresholds (ft-lb or % change) for knee/ankle/trunk: none; the pre-mission strength table is deadlift/bench press x body weight.
Reference means/SDs needed to turn the generator's g/cm2 into T-scores: not in the fetched documents.
